districts.notes: en.wiki 'Abu Ghraib District' article (Arabic: قضاء أبي غريب) lists cities, not nahiya; subdistrict grouping per COSIT via citypopulation.de. An-Nasir & As-Salam (النصر والسلام) covers Al Nasr Wal Salam area.
COSIT via citypopulation.de groups 4 nahiya here. Note: 2024-census data promotes Ar-Rashidiyah and Az-Zahur to separate districts; kept in Adhamiyah per the established structure.
COSIT via citypopulation.de groups 3 nahiya here (central Karkh + Al-Ma'mun + Al-Mansur).

COSIT via citypopulation.de groups 3 nahiya here (central Kadhimiya + At-Taji + Dhat as-Salasil). Note: 2024-census data renames/splits At-Taji into 'Fada al-Kadhimiya' district and Dhat as-Salasil into 'Sama al-Kadhimiya' district; kept under Kadhimiya per the established structure.
COSIT via citypopulation.de groups 3 nahiya here (central Mada'in + Al-Jisr + Al-Wahdah).
COSIT via citypopulation.de groups 4 nahiya here (central Mahmudiya + Al-Latifiyah + Al-Yusufiyah + Ar-Rashid).

COSIT via citypopulation.de groups 4 nahiya here (central Rusafa + Al-Karadah ash-Sharqiyah + Baghdad al-Jadidah + Falastin). Note: 2024-census data carves part of Rusafa (with parts of Sadr 1/2) into a new Az-Zawra' district; kept per the established structure.
District name per ar.wiki قضاء الصدر الأول; COSIT nahiya name is الصدر الأولى (Aṣ-Ṣadr al-Ūlā). Comprises 3 nahiya per citypopulation.de (COSIT).
District name per ar.wiki قضاء الصدر الثاني; COSIT nahiya name is الصدر الثانية (Aṣ-Ṣadr ath-Thāniyah). Comprises 3 nahiya per citypopulation.de (COSIT).

Arabic قضاء الطارمية confirmed via mapcarta/Wikidata and COSIT. Comprises 3 nahiya per citypopulation.de (central Tarmia + Al-Aba'iji + Al-Mushahidah). Note: en.wiki 'Al Tarmia' town article infobox erroneously says 'Salah al-Din Governorate' though its text says Baghdad Governorate.

governorates.notes: DISCREPANCIES: (1) en.wikipedia 'Districts of Iraq' lists 10 qada'a for Baghdad (used here as the official structure): Abu Ghraib, Al-Adhamiyah, Al-Karkh, Kadhimiya, Al-Mada'in, Mahmudiya, Al-Rasafa, Sadr City 1, Sadr City 2, Al Tarmia. (2) The en.wiki 'Baghdad Governorate' article instead lists 10 MUNICIPAL/Amanat units (Adhamiyah, Karkh, Karrada, Kadhimiya, Mansour, Sadr City, Al-Rashid, Al-Rusafa, New Baghdad, Al-Ghazaliya) — these are the 2003-era city kati'/district advisory councils under Amanat Baghdad, not qada'a; Karrada, Mansour, New Baghdad, Al-Rashid, Al-Ghazaliya are not qada'a. (3) ar.wikipedia 'أقضية العراق' lists 14 qada'a (adds Sha'ab, Al-Husayniyah (created 2013), Az-Zawra' (created 2018), Ash-Sha'lah) — newer official splits not yet reflected on en.wiki. (4) citypopulation.de's 2024-census update shows a newer COSIT reorganization: Az-Zahur, Ar-Rashidiyah, Az-Zawra', Fada' al-Kadhimiyah (At-Taji), and Sama al-Kadhimiyah (Dhat as-Salasil) now appear as separate districts; this dataset keeps the established 10-district structure. Subdistrict groupings per district were taken from citypopulation.de district pages (COSIT data); Wikipedia's own district articles do not list nahiya. Arabic spellings normalized to standard Arabic orthography.

districts.notes: ar.wiki Ramadi article intro lists nawahi Al-Yarmouk, Al-Wafa, Al-Rahhaliyah plus the center; its admin section names 3 (center, Rahhaliyah, Wafa). A dedicated article confirms ناحية اليرموك (aka Zankura) as a Ramadi nahiya with 2018 population data. The official subdistrict list shows only center + Wafa - possibly outdated.

Al-Karmah and Al-Amiriyah were formerly nawahi of Fallujah and are now listed as separate districts (see their notes). Saqlawiyah was voted to district status by the Anbar provincial council in 2017 per its ar.wiki article, but the official subdistrict list still shows ناحية الصقلاوية under Fallujah.
Confirmed by both the ar.wiki Hit article (table of administrative units) and the official subdistrict list.
Current separate district; confirmed by ar.wiki Haditha article (nawahi table, 2018 data) and the official subdistrict list. Older sources placing Haditha under Anah are outdated.

ar.wiki Anah article explicitly states the district has 4 nawahi (Anah, Al-Rayhaniyah, Hasa, Al-Sakrah) per 2013 census; the official subdistrict list shows only the district center - possible outdated data. Used the 4-nahiya list with this caveat.
Was a nahiya of Anah District until elevated to a district in 2001 (per ar.wiki). No subdistricts found in any source; only the district center is listed officially.

Official subdistrict list: center + Al-Ubur + Al-Ubaidi. ناحية العبور is the Rumana (الرمانة) area - the Sept 2019 provincial-council vote to create قضاء الرمانة was apparently not ratified, as official lists still show it as a nahiya of Al-Qa'im. Al-Karabila is described as a nahiya of Al-Qa'im in its ar.wiki article ('مدينة وناحية عراقية في قضاء القائم') but is absent from the official subdistrict list; included with this caveat. A dedicated article confirms ناحية العبيدي as an Al-Qa'im nahiya.
Nawahi Al-Waleed and Al-Nukhayb confirmed by both the official subdistrict list and a University of Anbar study.

NEW district (not in en.wiki's 8). Formerly ناحية الكرمة under Fallujah; ar.wiki Fallujah article (citing a 2026 academic study) says it is now a district, and the ar.wiki Al-Karmah article states it has nawahi Al-Khayrat and Al-Jazira. Caveat: the official subdistrict list still places ناحية الكرمة under Fallujah.

NEW district (not in en.wiki's 8). Formerly a nahiya of Fallujah; appears as قضاء العامرية (centered on عامرية الفلوجة) in ar.wiki's district lists and the official subdistrict list. No nawahi found - only the district center is listed officially.

NEW district (not in en.wiki's 8) - this is the 'Khalidiya' district discrepancy: officially قضاء الحبانية (Al-Habbaniyah District) centered on Al-Khalidiya city per ar.wiki; citypopulation.de, IOM DTM, and Iraqi statistics list it as Khalidiya, and Iraqi media call it قضاء الخالدية with its own qaimmaqam. Official subdistrict list shows only the district center; ar.wiki also documents a recently created ناحية السلام (جزيرة الخالدية) within this district.

governorates.notes: Official district count is disputed. en.wikipedia 'Districts of Iraq' lists 8 districts; ar.wikipedia (محافظة الأنبار, أقضية العراق) and the official-statistics-based 'قائمة نواحي العراق' show 10-11. The 3 newer districts included here: (1) Al-Amiriyah (العامرية) - appears as a district in the official subdistrict list; formerly a nahiya of Fallujah. (2) Khalidiya - this is the district listed by citypopulation.de, IOM DTM, and Iraqi statistics; officially قضاء الحبانية (Al-Habbaniyah District) centered on Al-Khalidiya city, and Iraqi media call it قضاء الخالدية with its own qaimmaqam. (3) Al-Karmah (الكرمة) - ar.wiki's Fallujah article (citing a 2026 academic study of administrative changes) says it is now a district with nawahi Al-Khayrat and Al-Jazira, though the official subdistrict list still places ناحية الكرمة under Fallujah. EXCLUDED (insufficient corroboration): قضاء الصقلاوية (2017 Anbar provincial-council vote to elevate Saqlawiyah nahiya; still listed as a Fallujah nahiya officially) and قضاء الرمانة (3 Sept 2019 provincial-council vote to elevate ناحية العبور/الرمانة; still listed as ناحية العبور under Al-Qa'im officially). Haditha is currently its own district; older sources placing Haditha under Anah District are outdated. No Kurdish names are in use in Anbar (Sunni Arab-majority governorate).

districts.notes: Subdistrict Al-Awja confirmed by ar.wiki 'قضاء تكريت' ('يتبع للقضاء إدارياً ناحية العوجة'). No other nahiya found; مقاطعات Malha, Al-Zulaya, Awinat are agricultural sub-units (مقاطعات), not nahiyas.

ar.wiki 'قضاء سامراء': 'يضم ثلاث نواحي هي المعتصم والثرثار ودجلة'. Note: a 2026 news item cited on ar.wiki's Tikrit page reported an attempt to annex Tikrit-area مقاطعات (Malha, Al-Zulaya, Awinat) to ناحية دجلة; no completed change documented.

ar.wiki 'قضاء بلد' lists الإسحاقي and يثرب as administrative units of the district; ar.wiki Saladin Governorate page states الضلوعية is 'ناحية تتبع قضاء بلد'. Yathrib as a Balad subdistrict is also confirmed by a Jan-2021 IMPACT/REACH factsheet ('Yathreb Subdistrict of Balad District').
ar.wiki 'قضاء بيجي' ('المدن والنواحي' section): الصينية، الزوية، ناحية مكحول.

ar.wiki 'قضاء الدور': since 1987 the district has no nahiyas other than ناحية المركز (district-centre subdistrict); former subdistricts Hamrin (حمرين) and Abu Dilf (أبو دلف) were abolished in 1987. Subdistrict list therefore left empty (markaz-only district).
ar.wiki 'قضاء الشرقاط' lists نواحي آشور، السهل الأخضر، تلول الباج (with population/area table).

ar.wiki 'قضاء طوز خورماتو' lists الطوز (مركز القضاء)، سليمان بيك، ينكجة، آمرلي — but آمرلي was promoted to qada'a in January 2017 (ar.wiki 'آمرلي'), so it is listed here as a district instead of a Tuz subdistrict. Subdistricts retained: Sulaiman Bek, Yankjah. en.wiki uses the name 'Tooz District'.

Previously known as Al-Faris (الفارس) — en.wiki 'Dujail District' ('formerly, Al-Faris'); ar.wiki 'قضاء الدجيل' ('سابقا: قضاء الفارس'). This explains IOM DTM's 'Al-Fares' district listing. Verified subdistrict: Al-Sheikh Jamil (الشيخ جميل) — ar.wiki 'قضاء الدجيل' plus an IOP Conference Series study (2023) locating a site in 'Salah Al-Din Province, Al-Dujail District, Al-Sheikh Jamil District'. ar.wiki's Dujail page also claims ناحية الثرثار, but that conflicts with ar.wiki's Samarra page (which documents Al-Tharthar as a Samarra subdistrict with stats); excluded as likely error.

Verified as qada'a (ar.wiki 'قضاء العلم': 'قضاء العلم هو قضاء في محافظة صلاح الدين'). Previously associated with Tikrit district (infobox on the page lists القضاء: تكريت, reflecting its older status as ناحية العلم, created 1962, later upgraded). No nahiya list found on the page or elsewhere — only villages listed; subdistrict list left empty.

Verified as qada'a: ar.wiki 'آمرلي' ('المستوى الإداري: قضاء') states it was a nahiya of Tuz Khurmatu until January 2017, when it was promoted to district. Predominantly Turkmen (Turkman-speaking, Shia) population — not Kurdish. The page lists villages but no nahiyas; subdistrict list left empty.

governorates.notes: DISTRICT-COUNT DISCREPANCY: en.wikipedia.org ('Districts of Iraq' and 'Saladin Governorate') lists 8 districts, but Iraq's Central Statistical Organization (as published on citypopulation.de) lists 10. The two additions are Al-Alam (العلم) and Amirli (آمرلي), both verified as qada'a: ar.wikipedia's 'قضاء العلم' page explicitly calls Al-Alam a qada'a of Saladin (created as a nahiya in 1962, later upgraded), and the ar.wikipedia 'آمرلي' page states Amirli was promoted from nahiya to qada'a in January 2017 (it had been a subdistrict of Tuz Khurmatu). Both are therefore included here. IOM DTM reports list an 'Al-Fares' district — this is Dujail, which was previously known as Al-Faris (الفارس); confirmed by en.wiki 'Dujail District' ('formerly, Al-Faris') and ar.wiki 'قضاء الدجيل' ('سابقا: قضاء الفارس'). Al-Tharthar (الثرثار) naming conflict: ar.wiki's Dujail page claims Dujail includes 'ناحية الثرثار', but ar.wiki's Samarra page documents ناحية الثرثار (with 1997/2012 population and area stats) as a Samarra subdistrict; Dujail's claim appears erroneous, so Al-Tharthar is listed only under Samarra.
